# Shipped definitions

**Role:** reference
**Status:** generated by `python -m femkit schema docs` — do not edit
**Authority:** none of its own; the schema models are the authority for `femkit/data/` (definitions.md)

## ControlDefinition

`femkit/data/channels.txt` and `control.txt` — the channel order, and the control environment's packages as `conda create --file` reads them (definitions.md § 3).

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `channels` | list of text | required | channels.txt: the channel order every environment is solved with, one bare channel name a line |
| `dependencies` | list of text | required | control.txt: conda package constraints; exactly one `python=X.Y` |

## EnvironmentDefinition

`femkit/data/environments/<name>.toml` — one environment: an engine's (definitions.md § 4), or a tool's, which states its `version_command` instead of an `engine` (§ 4.7).

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `engine` | text, optional | — | the registered engine adapter ID; absent for a tool environment |
| `version_command` | list of text, optional | — | a tool environment's: the command, run in the prefix, whose last line of output is its version |
| `version` | text | required | what the version probe must report |
| `control_packages` | boolean | `false` | a tool environment's: the control environment's packages (control.txt), solved with its own (definitions.md § 4.7) |
| `description` | text | required | one line for `env list` |
| `default` | boolean | `false` | part of `env install --all` |
| `thread_variables` | list of text | empty | variables set to a run's threads per rank |
| `fixed_variables` | table of text → text | empty | variables set to these values in every check and run |
| `toolchain` | [Toolchain](#toolchain), optional | — | the compilers and build tools its builds use; required with builds |
| `packages` | [Packages](#packages) | see table | what the manager solves; in the environments the catalogue builds, the toolchain's packages are added to `conda` |
| `provides` | [Provides](#provides) | see table | what the install's audit step finds inside the prefix |
| `cuda` | [CudaPart](#cudapart), optional | — | what the CUDA environment, `&lt;name&gt;-cuda`, adds; absent: there is none |
| `sources` | list of [Source](#source) | empty | pinned source archives |
| `builds` | list of [Build](#build) | empty | CMake builds; each installs after the builds its `after` names |
| `checks` | list of [Check](#check) | empty | the checks that prove an install |
| `agreements` | table of text → [Agreement](#agreement) | empty | agreement group -&gt; what must agree |

## Toolchain

`[toolchain]` — the compilers and build tools this environment's builds use, solved into it and proven before any source is fetched (definitions.md § 4.6). Each environment declares its own: environments may need different compilers, versions or patches.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `packages` | list of text | required | conda constraints: the compilers, the sysroot and every tool a build calls, solved with the environment's packages |
| `tools` | list of text | required | executables a build calls; each must resolve inside the prefix |
| `compilers` | table of text → text | required | language (c, cxx, fortran) -&gt; the variable the activation sets to its compiler; at least one |
| `mpi` | table of text → text | empty | language -&gt; the MPI compiler wrapper the environment provides, for a language `compilers` names; when declared, the toolchain check builds with them and runs two ranks |

## Packages

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `conda` | list of text | empty | conda constraints the manager solves |
| `pip` | list of text | empty | Python packages conda-forge does not have; not built yet, so an environment that lists one does not load (definitions.md § 4.1) |
| `forbid` | list of text | empty | package families that must be absent from the solved lock |

## Provides

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `executables` | list of text | empty | executables the install's audit step finds in the prefix |
| `modules` | list of text | empty | Python modules the install's audit step imports |

## CudaPart

`[cuda]` — what the definition's CUDA environment, `<name>-cuda`, adds to it (definitions.md § 4.5); the other environment is the definition without it.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | text | required | what the CUDA build is for, appended to the description in `env list` |
| `packages` | list of text | empty | conda constraints solved only with CUDA |
| `executables` | list of text | empty | executables the audit finds only with CUDA |
| `sources` | list of [Source](#source) | empty | pinned sources only the CUDA environment builds |
| `builds` | list of [Build](#build) | empty | builds only the CUDA environment has; a build of the definition may name one in `after` |

## Source

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | text | required | the source's ID, referenced by builds as `{source:&lt;id&gt;}` |
| `archive` | text | required | URL of the archive of exactly `commit` |
| `sha256` | text | required | SHA-256 of the archive |
| `commit` | text | required | the upstream commit the archive holds |
| `release` | text | required | the upstream release name of that commit |
| `into` | text | required | where the archive is unpacked, under the prefix's source tree |
| `version_text` | text, optional | — | stands in for `git describe` where the build asks git for a version |

## Build

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | text | required | the build's ID |
| `source` | text | required | the source it builds |
| `after` | list of text | empty | builds that must be installed first |
| `cuda_architectures` | boolean | `false` | in the CUDA environment, compiled for `build.cuda_architectures` |
| `rpath` | list of text | empty | install RPATH entries, relative to the prefix |
| `options` | table of text → Any | empty | CMake cache entries; a boolean becomes BOOL, anything else STRING. Strings may use placeholders. Placeholders: `{build}`, `{prefix}`, `{source}` |
| `cuda_options` | table of text → Any | empty | CMake cache entries added in the CUDA environment; in the other, each boolean among them is set false and the rest are left out. Placeholders: `{build}`, `{prefix}`, `{source}` |

## Check

One bounded calculation and the numbers it must produce (definitions.md § 5).

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | text | required | the check's ID |
| `kind` | `command` \| `ctest` \| `pytest` | required | how it runs (definitions.md § 5.1) |
| `run` | list of text, optional | — | command: the program and its arguments. Placeholders: `{prefix}`, `{ranks}`, `{threads}`, `{work}` |
| `build` | text, optional | — | ctest: the build whose test tree holds the test |
| `test` | text, optional | — | ctest: the test's name |
| `source` | text, optional | — | pytest: the source tree holding the tests |
| `tests` | list of text | empty | pytest: the test node IDs, relative to the source tree |
| `plugins` | list of text | empty | pytest: modules loaded first, as `-p` plugins (e.g. mpi4py.MPI, so MPI starts before the tests import an MPI build) |
| `ranks` | integer | `1` | MPI ranks |
| `threads` | integer | `1` | threads per rank |
| `read` | text | required | the reader ID that turns its output into quantities |
| `expect` | table of text → [Expectation](#expectation) | empty | quantity -&gt; its bounds |
| `agree` | text, optional | — | the agreement group it belongs to |
| `device` | boolean | `false` | uses a GPU: exists only in the CUDA environment, and runs only with `env validate --gpu` |
| `upstream_verdict` | boolean | `true` | ctest: the test's own pass or fail counts, besides `expect`; false where its stored reference does not hold for the pinned libraries — the definition says why — and only `expect` decides |
| `timeout` | integer | `600` | seconds before it is stopped |

## Expectation

What one quantity must be. At least one bound is given; a bound is a finite number, since an infinite one would bound nothing.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `min` | number, optional | — | the smallest value allowed |
| `max` | number, optional | — | the largest value allowed |
| `equals` | number or integer or text, optional | — | the exact value required |

## Agreement

Checks that must give the same quantity (definitions.md § 5.2).

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quantity` | text | required | the quantity compared |
| `rtol` | number | required | relative tolerance, element-wise for a list; finite |

## ManagerKind

`femkit/data/managers/<kind>.toml` — how to drive one package manager (definitions.md § 6). The kind's name is the file stem, and is the manager executable's name.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `version` | list of text | required | prints the manager's version. Placeholders: `{exe}`, `{file}`, `{prefix}` |
| `version_pattern` | text | required | regular expression whose first group is the version in that output |
| `root` | [JsonQuery](#jsonquery) | required | where the manager's root (base) prefix is |
| `platform` | [JsonQuery](#jsonquery), optional | — | the platform an environment built by this manager is for, e.g. linux-64 (jobs.md § 9.1) |
| `run` | list of text | required | runs the command that follows inside {prefix}. Placeholders: `{exe}`, `{file}`, `{prefix}` |
| `activate` | [Activation](#activation) | required | how a shell enters a prefix: the day-to-day entry line, the run script |
| `create` | list of text | required | creates {prefix} from constraints, overriding the person's own channels and default packages; `channel` follows once per channel, then the constraints — for the control environment, `--file` and its package list. Placeholders: `{exe}`, `{file}`, `{prefix}` |
| `channel` | list of text | required | the arguments that add one channel, e.g. ["-c", "{channel}"] |
| `create_from_lock` | list of text | required | creates {prefix} from the exact package list in {file}. Placeholders: `{exe}`, `{file}`, `{prefix}` |
| `export_lock` | list of text | required | prints the exact package list of {prefix}, one URL a line. Placeholders: `{exe}`, `{file}`, `{prefix}` |
| `remove` | list of text | required | removes {prefix}. Placeholders: `{exe}`, `{file}`, `{prefix}` |
| `channels_named` | list of `create_from_lock` \| `remove` | empty | the commands beside `create` that name the declared channels, `channel` once per channel after the command: conda 26 otherwise checks the terms of its base configuration's defaults and stops; mamba 2.9.0 refuses channels on a removal (both measured, envs.md § 4.4) |

## JsonQuery

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `argv` | list of text | required | the command; it prints one JSON object. Placeholders: `{exe}`, `{file}`, `{prefix}` |
| `key` | text or list of text | required | the key of the object that holds the answer; a list: the first of them the object has, where versions of a manager differ |

## Activation

The two ways a shell enters a prefix with this manager; this machine's activation.command chooses one (config.md § 3.1; envs.md § 6.2).

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hook` | text | required | the file whose sourcing defines the activation in a fresh shell, under {root} (the manager's root query); checked on disk, never derived from the executable's path, which on a cluster may be a module's wrapper. Placeholders: `{root}` |
| `with_hook` | list of text | required | the shell function, e.g. `conda activate {prefix}`: it exists once the hook is sourced, which femkit does first. Placeholders: `{prefix}` |
| `without_hook` | list of text | required | the activate script on PATH, `source activate {prefix}`, which needs no hook — what a cluster's module provides. Placeholders: `{prefix}` |

## SchedulerKind

`femkit/data/schedulers/<kind>.toml` — how to talk to one scheduler (jobs.md § 7). A kind with commands is detected on a machine when its `submit` command is found.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `commands` | table of text → text | empty | role (submit, query, cancel, cluster) -&gt; the command's usual name; the probe records where each is found or declared |
| `probe` | table of text → text | empty | role -&gt; a command that measures a machine of this kind; the roles are its reader's, in femkit/schedulers/, and checked against it when the kind loads |
| `mpi_launch` | list of text | required | the launcher `config init` proposes for `launch.mpi` on a machine of this kind. Placeholders: `{ranks}` |
| `job_variables` | table of text → text | empty | role (id, ranks, cores_per_rank, cores_on_node, gpus, nodes) -&gt; the variable a job sees; `id` set means the process runs inside a job |
| `interactive` | text, optional | — | the command that opens an interactive allocation, named by bootstrap's login-node warning and when an install step on a login node of this kind is killed (envs.md § 6.2); never with a partition |

## UnitTable

The units a value may be written in (`femkit/data/units.toml`).

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dimensions` | table of text → text | required | each base dimension and its canonical unit, as written; every value of the dimension is held in it |
| `prefixes` | table of text → integer | required | each SI prefix and its power of ten |
| `units` | table of text → [UnitEntry](#unitentry) | required | each unit symbol, in order: an `equals` may use only the units above it |

## UnitEntry

One unit: a base dimension times an exact factor, or an expression of units above it.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dimension` | text, optional | — | the base dimension this unit measures, when it is defined by one; with `factor` |
| `factor` | text | `"1"` | with `dimension`: how many of the dimension's canonical unit one of this unit is, an exact number (`1/1000`) |
| `equals` | text, optional | — | otherwise: what one of this unit is, an expression of units above it (`W/A`, `1.602176634e-19 J`) |
| `prefixes` | boolean | required | whether SI prefixes apply to it (`nm`, `kV`) |

## FormulationDefinition

One physical problem, stated without reference to any engine (models.md § 4).

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | text | required | one line: what it solves |
| `science` | text | required | its science document, from the checkout's root |
| `unknown` | [Unknown](#unknown) | required | what it solves for |
| `meanings` | table of `2` \| `3` → list of text | required | what each dimension may mean; a model chooses one |
| `conventions` | list of `phasor` \| `amplitude` | empty | the conventions a model must choose |
| `constants` | table of text → [Constant](#constant) | empty | the physical constants its equation uses, each given to every engine as stated here |
| `properties` | table of text → [PropertySpec](#propertyspec) | required | the material properties it reads |
| `conditions` | table of text → [KindSpec](#kindspec) | required | the condition kinds it allows |
| `sources` | table of text → [KindSpec](#kindspec) | empty | the source kinds it allows |
| `derived` | table of text → [DerivedSpec](#derivedspec) | required | each quantity an observable may name |
| `benchmarks` | table of text → [Benchmark](#benchmark) | empty | its benchmark set: problems with known answers (models.md § 6.3) |

## Unknown

What the formulation solves for.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | text | required | its name (`potential`) |
| `space` | `H1` \| `Hcurl` | required | its function space |
| `unit` | text | required | its unit |

## Constant

A physical constant the formulation's equation uses, as every engine must be given it.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | text | required | one plain sentence: what it is or states |
| `section` | text | required | the science document's section that defines it, as its link anchor (`3-conditions-on-an-outer-boundary`) |
| `value` | text | required | its value, with its unit |

## PropertySpec

A material property the formulation reads.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | text | required | one plain sentence: what it is or states |
| `section` | text | required | the science document's section that defines it, as its link anchor (`3-conditions-on-an-outer-boundary`) |
| `unit` | text | required | its unit; `1` for a plain number |
| `complex` | boolean | required | whether its values may be complex |

## KindSpec

A condition or source kind: where it may stand, and its parameters.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | text | required | one plain sentence: what it is or states |
| `section` | text | required | the science document's section that defines it, as its link anchor (`3-conditions-on-an-outer-boundary`) |
| `on` | list of `domain` \| `boundary` \| `interface` | required | the region kinds it may be stated on |
| `parameters` | table of text → [ParameterSpec](#parameterspec) | empty | each parameter |

## ParameterSpec

One parameter of a condition or source.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `unit` | text | required | its unit |
| `description` | text | required | one plain sentence: what the value is |

## DerivedSpec

A quantity an observable may name.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | text | required | one plain sentence: what it is or states |
| `section` | text | required | the science document's section that defines it, as its link anchor (`3-conditions-on-an-outer-boundary`) |
| `unit` | text | required | its unit |

## Benchmark

A problem with a known answer (models.md § 4, § 6.3): a project of its own, and the exact value each of its observables must reproduce.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | text | required | one plain sentence: what it is or states |
| `section` | text | required | the science document's section that defines it, as its link anchor (`3-conditions-on-an-outer-boundary`) |
| `project` | text | required | its folder, from femkit/data/formulations/, holding model.toml and study.toml |
| `exercises` | list of text | required | the formulation's condition, source and property kinds it exercises |
| `tolerance` | text | required | the relative difference a run may show from each reference value, a plain number; its basis is in the science document's section |
| `reference` | table of text → text | required | each observable of its study, and its exact value |

## MesherDefinition

One mesher (models.md § 6.5).

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | text | required | one line |
| `provided_by` | text | required | the engine environment it runs in |
| `dimensions` | list of `2` \| `3` | required | the dimensions it meshes |
| `builds` | list of text | required | the model's shape kinds it can build |
| `imports` | list of `step` \| `iges` \| `brep` \| `stl` | empty | the CAD formats an `import` may be in |
| `controls` | list of `size` \| `regions` | required | the mesh policy's keys it honors |
| `tolerance` | [Tolerance](#tolerance), optional | — | its geometric tolerance; absent: not known, and no feature can be checked against it |
| `writes` | [Writes](#writes) | required | the mesh it writes |
| `orders` | list of integer | required | the geometry orders it writes |
| `keeps_region_names` | boolean | required | whether the mesh's parts keep the model's region names |
| `basis` | text | required | where these facts come from: what was measured, on which version, or a citation |

## Tolerance

How close two points must be for the mesher to merge them.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `absolute` \| `relative` | required | in the length unit geometry is handed over in, or relative to the model's size |
| `value` | text | required | a plain number |

## Writes

The mesh file it writes.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `format` | text | required | the format (`msh`, `vol`) |
| `version` | text, optional | — | the format's version, where it has several |
| `encoding` | `ascii` \| `binary`, optional | — | text or binary |

## Page

`femkit/data/web/page.toml`.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema` | `1` | required | this file's shape; raised when it changes |
| `app` | [App](#app) | required |  |
| `workspaces` | list of [Workspace](#workspace) | required |  |
| `context` | list of [ContextPart](#contextpart) | required |  |
| `kinds` | table of text → text | required | each object type's icon (models.md § 11.2) |
| `shortcuts` | list of [Shortcut](#shortcut) | empty |  |

## App

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | text | required | what the page is called |
| `tagline` | text | required | what femkit is, in one sentence |
| `mark` | text | required | its mark, a file the page ships |

## Workspace

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | text | required | how the address names it |
| `title` | text | required | what a person reads on it |
| `icon` | text | required | its icon, by the icon set's name |
| `tagline` | text | required | what it is, in one sentence |
| `help` | text | required | how it is used |
| `document` | text, optional | — | the read-only operation whose answer it shows; none: the registry itself |
| `context` | list of `project` \| `study` \| `environment` | empty | the context it needs |
| `empty` | text | required | what it says before there is anything to show |

## ContextPart

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | `project` \| `study` \| `environment` | required |  |
| `label` | text | required | what a person reads beside it |
| `help` | text | required | what it is |
| `choices` | text | required | the read-only operation that lists its choices |
| `rows` | text | required | the field of that operation's result holding the choices |
| `value_key` | text, optional | — | each row's key holding the choice; none: the row is it |
| `label_key` | text, optional | — | each row's key a person reads; none: the value |
| `depends` | list of `project` \| `study` \| `environment` | empty | what must be chosen first |

## Shortcut

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | text | required | the key, `Mod` the platform's command key |
| `command` | `undo` \| `redo` \| `remove` \| `commit` \| `cancel` | required | the page's command it runs |
| `help` | text | required | what it does |
